Welcome to our Frequently Asked Questions page! Here, you'll find answers to some of the most common queries about planning and enjoying your safari adventure in Tanzania. To view an answer, simply click on the question that interests you. If your question isn't listed here, our professional local team is more than happy to assist you further. We're committed to making your safari experience seamless and unforgettable. Please do not hesitate to reach out for personalised assistance and information.

What is the best time to visit Tanzania for a safari?

The best time to visit Tanzania for a safari is during the dry season, from late June to October. This period offers the best wildlife viewing opportunities as animals congregate around water sources. However, for those interested in witnessing the Great Migration, the best time would be from late January to February when the calving season occurs in the Serengeti.

Read more

What types of safari packages do you offer?

We offer a variety of safari packages tailored to different interests and budgets, including luxury safaris, budget safaris, family-friendly safaris, and photographic safaris. Each package includes professional guides, accommodation, and transport. Customized itineraries are also available to match specific interests such as bird watching or big cat tracking.

Read more

Are your safaris suitable for families with children?

Yes, our safaris are family-friendly, and we provide special accommodations and activities suitable for children. Our guides are experienced in engaging with young explorers, making the safari experience educational and enjoyable for all ages. We recommend children be at least six years old for optimal enjoyment and safety.

Read more

What should I pack for a safari in Tanzania?

Packing for a safari should include light, breathable clothing with neutral colors, a warm jacket for early morning game drives, a sun hat, sunglasses, sunscreen, a good pair of binoculars, and a camera. It’s also advisable to bring personal medications and a basic first aid kit. Mosquito repellent and malaria prophylaxis are recommended.

Read more

Do I need any vaccinations before traveling to Tanzania?

Yes, visitors to Tanzania are recommended to have vaccinations for hepatitis A, typhoid, and polio, as well as a yellow fever vaccination if coming from a country with risk of yellow fever. Malaria prophylaxis is also recommended. It’s best to consult with a travel doctor well in advance of your trip.

Read more

What kind of wildlife can I expect to see on a safari?

Tanzania is home to a diverse range of wildlife including the Big Five: elephant, lion, leopard, buffalo, and rhinoceros. You can also expect to see cheetahs, giraffes, hyenas, wildebeest, zebras, and numerous bird species. Each park has its own unique ecosystem offering different viewing opportunities.

Read more

Are Safari Holidays Safe ?

Yes, safari holidays are safe when organised with reputable and experienced safari operators like Mazingira Safaris. We ensure the safety of our guests by providing experienced guides, maintaining well-equipped vehicles, adhering strictly to park regulations, and conducting comprehensive pre-trip safety briefings. We also have robust emergency response plans in place, including access to medical care. Our commitment to safety allows you to enjoy the breathtaking beauty of the wilderness with peace of mind.

Read more

Can I use credit cards during my trip?

Major hotels and lodges accept credit cards; however, it’s advisable to carry some cash in USD or Tanzanian shillings for small purchases, tips, and in areas where credit cards are not accepted. ATMs are available in larger towns and cities but can be scarce in remote areas.

Read more

How many days do I need for a Tanzania safari ?

The ideal length for a Tanzania safari can vary depending on your interests and the areas you wish to explore, but generally, a safari of 7 to 10 days allows for a comprehensive experience. This duration provides ample time to visit multiple parks like the Serengeti, Ngorongoro Crater, and Tarangire National Park, each offering unique landscapes and wildlife. For those who also want to include a visit to Zanzibar or other cultural sites, extending the trip to 12-14 days is recommended to enjoy a relaxed pace and a broader exploration of Tanzania's diverse attractions.

Read more

How much does a Tanzania safari cost?

The cost of a safari in Tanzania can vary widely based on the duration of the trip, the type of accommodation, the season, and whether the safari is private or group-based. Generally, prices can range from $200 to over $1000 per person per day.

Read more

What are the accommodation options on a safari?

Accommodation options range from luxury lodges and tented camps to more basic campsites. Many safari packages include accommodations that offer a comfortable and authentic wilderness experience.
